channel.title: Crisp & Counter
channel.description: Plain-language buying guides for countertop cooking appliances.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: The two shapes are not rivals in the same contest. They solve different problems, and most buying regret comes from picking the shape that solves the other person's problem.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: The quart number on the box is the least useful number on the box. Here is what to compare instead, and why two machines with the same figure can hold very different dinners.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: The appliance you stop using is the one that is annoying to clean or annoying to store. Both are decidable before purchase, from the listing, if you know which lines to read.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.category: Buy the function, not the badge
item.description: “24 presets” and “multi-function” are counts, not capabilities. Here is how to find out which functions you will actually use before you pay for the rest.

item.title: Thanksgiving overflow: what an air fryer actually fixes on the biggest oven day
item.description: It will not roast the turkey. What it can do is take four sides, the rolls and the reheating off an oven that is already holding a bird for four hours. Here is the plan, and the questions to ask a listing before you believe it.

item.title: Frozen food nights: four questions that decide whether a basket earns its counter
item.description: Most air-fryer purchases are justified on weeknights, not weekends. Before you buy one for the freezer aisle, four questions are worth answering with your own kitchen in front of you.

item.title: Dual basket or two separate machines? The counter math nobody writes down
item.description: Two baskets in one box looks obviously better than one. The comparison that matters is against two small single-basket machines — on outlets, on cleanup, on cooking floor, and on what happens when one half breaks.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in probe? Two thermometers, one question
item.description: Two of the five links in our register are not air fryers at all — one is a wired multi-probe set, one is a one-second handheld. Same treatment as the fryers: what each listing claims, which question decides it, and what neither can tell you.

item.title: Your first week with a new air fryer: a checklist that is not recipes
item.description: Everything you should do in the first seven days so the appliance is still on the counter in month six — seasoning the run, learning the hot spots, and setting up the cleanup you will actually keep.
